clue.text: Inspector Salteena, for one, having a better spell

indicators.note: a better spelling corrects a misspelt word, so one wrong letter is swapped for the right one

parts.note: Mr Salteena is a character in Daisy Ashford's The Young Visiters, whose title keeps the child author's misspelling

explanation.surface: A police inspector with an odd name turns out to be a better speller than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Ashford wrote The Young Visiters aged nine; Mr Salteena is one of its visiters, and spelling the word properly turns VISITER into VISITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is an official who calls to check an institution, such as a prison or hospital, which is what an inspector does.

clue.text: Invaders very taken with good book

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
1 Kings, written I Kings, is a book of the Good Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone is very taken with a good book they are reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good book' suggests a novel, but it points to the Bible, and the first book of Kings is written I Kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Norse raiders who invaded Britain and much of Europe from the eighth century.

clue.text: An isle, then, a curious place for Emperor

indicators.note: something curious is odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island turns out to be a strange spot for an emperor to end up.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is AN ISLE THEN A, so 'then' belongs to the anagram as well as reading like a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to the South Atlantic island of St Helena, where he died in 1821.

clue.text: Sacred book is in pieces

parts.note: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha
is shortened to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: A holy book has fallen apart.
explanation.walkthrough: TOBIT + 'S reads as 'Tobit is', and splits differently as TO BITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smashed to bits is broken into fragments, which is the state of being in pieces.

clue.text: Sign of top family's embarrassment, getting such a good hand

parts.note: the royal family is the top family in the land
a flush or blush is the sign of embarrassment
joins the two halves: the flush is the sign of embarrassment

explanation.surface: The royals go red with embarrassment at being dealt a fine hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal flush, ace to ten in one suit, is the best possible hand in poker.

clue.text: Expert help needed after poor return

indicators.note: after places the help piece behind the other piece rather than in front
to return is to go back, so the word for poor is read back to front

parts.note: poor quality is bad
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: After a poor result, you call in expert assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an informal British term for someone skilled at a particular task, an expert.

clue.text: Do graffiti, getting name round area

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
A is the usual abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A graffiti artist sprays their tag around a neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear paint crudely on a surface, which is what scrawling graffiti involves.

clue.text: Before lesson, pick up party hat

indicators.note: before says the party piece comes ahead of the lesson piece
in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party
the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: Before a class, a pupil collects a paper hat for the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, a kind of cap named after the royal castle.

clue.text: Girl one helps with speech

indicators.note: speech means the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: one who helps is an aider, said with a British accent that drops the final r

explanation.surface: A girl helps someone who has trouble speaking, like a speech therapist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sends you towards a speech therapist; in fact 'aider' said in a non-rhotic accent sounds just like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a girl's name, and crosswords freely use any first name to stand for girl.

clue.text: Concerned with food? Get it ready-cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms its ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: If you care about your meals, buy them ready-made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready-cooked' reads as one word for convenience food, but the hyphen splits it into the fodder and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet, the food a person eats.

clue.text: I agree to back swimmer

indicators.note: going back means running from the end towards the start, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to OK something is to agree to it

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to put money on a competitor in a swimming race.
explanation.definitionFit: The koi is an ornamental carp kept in ponds, a fish and so a swimmer.

clue.text: If I may pay for your holiday, say

definitions.note: the second definition gives the phrase as heard, BUY YOUR LEAVE

parts.note: first meaning: a polite request for permission

indicators.note: say means the phrase is to be spoken aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: to buy your leave would be to pay for your time off

explanation.surface: A generous host offers to pay for your holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: By your leave is an old-fashioned polite formula asking permission, just like if I may.

clue.text: A short denial

parts.note: surface reading: a brief, curt refusal
setter's reading: someone short is the opposite of someone tall, so describing a short person means denying that they are tall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like brief, but it means not tall; read as a phrase, 'not a tall' runs together into a firm denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying not at all is a firm way to deny or refuse something completely.

clue.text: Had tea? You've been had

parts.note: to have had something is to have got it
cha or char is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you have had your tea, then reveals it was a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'had' changes sense: first possession, then being fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotcha is the triumphant cry of someone who has caught you out or tricked you.

clue.text: Plant bed over springtime

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
on, as in resting on top of
Easter falls in spring

explanation.surface: A gardener plants out a flower bed once spring has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb telling you to sow, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a shrub with small leaves and red berries, common in gardens and hedges.

clue.text: Left followers in this penal institution

parts.note: Labour is the main left-wing party in British politics
a camp is a body of supporters, as in the Remain camp

explanation.surface: Supporters of the left are locked up in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: It hints at political prisoners, but it simply joins the party to the word for its supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour camp is a prison where inmates are forced to do hard physical work, so a penal institution.

clue.text: Killed in skid

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old past tense of slay
second meaning: to swing round or slide sideways out of control

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a report of a fatal road accident; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the archaic past tense of slay, and as a verb it also means to slide or swerve sideways.

clue.text: Decent public transport? That's a joke

parts.note: something decent is agreeable or pleasant
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A commuter scoffs at the idea of a decent bus or train service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a joke' sounds like a sneer at public transport, but 'joke' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light, good-humoured remark or jest made in conversation.

clue.text: Two colleges appear in table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: both Oxford and Cambridge universities have a college of this name
second meaning: a small table with drop leaves, named after an earl of the same title

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a league table of colleges; the name in fact belongs to a college at Oxford, another at Cambridge, and a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pembroke table is a small occasional table with hinged flaps, and Pembroke College exists at both Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Tin-openers deployed in inappropriate style

indicators.note: deployed means spread out into position, so these letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone uses tin-openers at a smart dinner, a breach of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretension is affected grandeur, a showy manner that claims more than is warranted and so is out of place.

clue.text: On foreshore road, catch up diver

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so one piece sits over the other
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to cop someone is to catch them
a hard is a firm roadway or landing place laid on a foreshore

explanation.surface: Walking along the beach road, you catch sight of a bird diving.
explanation.walkthrough: A hard is a paved slipway or track across a beach, mainly a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck, feeding by plunging underwater, so it is fairly called a diver.

clue.text: Boat fitted with new sort of nose

indicators.note: a vessel fitted with something has it installed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is a boat
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A boat gets a new nose cone fitted to its bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and turned up, so snub names a kind of nose.

clue.text: Infliction of violence as a source of power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the crime of hitting someone
second meaning: a cell that stores and supplies electricity

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a dictator's maxim that violence brings power; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery is the legal term for unlawful physical force against someone, and a battery also supplies electric power.

clue.text: Have duty to go through lines poet produced

indicators.note: passing through something puts you inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, here repeated for the plural
to owe something is to have a duty to pay or do it

explanation.surface: A poet whose job forces them to work through line after line of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is stretched to three Ls, with the debt word placed after the first of them; 'produced' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Lowell and James Russell Lowell were both American poets.

clue.text: Poet hard to decipher, for the most part

indicators.note: the most part of something is all of it but a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: crabbed handwriting is cramped and hard to read

explanation.surface: A poet's verse is mostly impossible to make sense of.
explanation.definitionFit: George Crabbe was an English poet of the late 18th and early 19th centuries, author of The Borough.

clue.text: Getting backs up with skill, ran in try over in the centre

definitions.note: describes behaviour that gets people's backs up, so an adjective

indicators.note: ran, taking in, holds the reversed try inside itself

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of cooking

indicators.note: goes in the centre means the built piece is set inside the skill word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned over means upended, so the word for try is read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A rugby team's backs show skill and run in a try in the middle of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture sends you to backs as players; 'in the centre' means the built piece goes into the middle of the skill word, just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant behaviour is haughty and overbearing, the kind that annoys people and gets their backs up.

clue.text: Jenny is a serving girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the small bird known as jenny ...
second meaning: a woman serving in the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a maid called Jenny; the two halves are a bird's nickname and a member of the women's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny wren is a traditional nickname for the bird, and a Wren is a member of the WRNS, the British women's naval service.

clue.text: Fit to half-inch

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to take for yourself, steal; half-inch is rhyming slang for pinch

explanation.walkthrough: Half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, which means to steal; the verb sense of the answer is to take without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriate as an adjective means suitable, and as a verb means to take something for your own use.

clue.text: Criticise sleep-over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for sleep is read the other way

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a child's sleepover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep-over' looks like the children's party; the hyphen splits it into sleep and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly, as reviewers do.

clue.text: Article afterwards shortened

indicators.note: something shortened has been cut, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: then means after that, afterwards

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is cut down later by the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: The is the definite article in English grammar.

clue.text: Cleric admitting worker's like poet

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the worker goes inside the cleric

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric of a cathedral
the worker ant; the 's reads as 'is' and is a link

explanation.surface: A clergyman lets in a labourer who is rather like a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker's' is 'worker is', so the 's joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dantean means in the manner of Dante, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Horse is companion to Norse god

parts.note: a pal is a friend or companion
Frey is the Norse god of fertility and fair weather

explanation.surface: A horse serves as companion to a Norse god, as Sleipnir did to Odin.
explanation.definitionFit: A palfrey is a gentle riding horse of the Middle Ages, often ridden by ladies.
